nodes.label: Branch protection stays a habit, not a technical rule (2026-10-14)
nodes.norm_label: branch protection stays a habit, not a technical rule (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: GitHub's technical branch protection costs money on a private repo via GitHub Pro, which is not worth it for a rule a one-person team already follows, since CI already catches regressions independently.

nodes.label: Testing instructions: unit tests in lib/, 4 critical e2e flows
nodes.norm_label: testing instructions: unit tests in lib/, 4 critical e2e flows

nodes.label: Lightweight process: slices, DoD, stop-and-ask conditions
nodes.norm_label: lightweight process: slices, dod, stop-and-ask conditions

nodes.label: Change size policy (relaxed 2026-11-07): no PR size limit
nodes.norm_label: change size policy (relaxed 2026-11-07): no pr size limit
nodes.rationale: The owner does not read diffs line by line; the safety net is the test suite, CI, and §9/§10 stop-and-ask boundaries, not small PRs, so slices can be grouped into large sessions/PRs.

nodes.label: Auth flow details and mail-free e2e login (task 1.1)
nodes.norm_label: auth flow details and mail-free e2e login (task 1.1)
nodes.rationale: Passwordless auth avoids reset/hash flows; link uses token_hash (not PKCE code) because email is often opened on a different device; e2e uses Supabase admin.generateLink to skip sending real mail.

nodes.label: Auth: magic link + Google OAuth, no passwords (2026-09-24)
nodes.norm_label: auth: magic link + google oauth, no passwords (2026-09-24)
nodes.rationale: No passwords avoids password reset and hash storage; Google is the fastest sign-in for most users.

nodes.label: Pure ranking function sorts offers by |offer ELO - viewer ELO| (task 3.8)
nodes.norm_label: pure ranking function sorts offers by |offer elo - viewer elo| (task 3.8)
nodes.rationale: Treating a missing ELO on either side as Infinity (not an exception) lets the same function cover a guest viewer by falling back to date-only sort without special-case code.

nodes.label: ELO ranking wired into the feed; viewer's own offers excluded, pagination moved to memory (task 3.9)
nodes.norm_label: elo ranking wired into the feed; viewer's own offers excluded, pagination moved to memory (task 3.9)
nodes.rationale: Correct 'Best match' on later pages requires sorting the whole filtered list before slicing it, so SQL offset pagination was replaced with in-memory sort appropriate for a single-city feed's size.

nodes.label: In-app notifications table added for a visible bell/inbox (2026-10-17)
nodes.norm_label: in-app notifications table added for a visible bell/inbox (2026-10-17)
nodes.rationale: Push only reaches subscribed users and email fallback without a verified domain only reaches the account owner, so a player with neither got nothing when accepted or messaged; an in-app bell doesn't depend on either channel.

nodes.label: RLS enabled on all tables, no policies: deny by default (2026-09-29)
nodes.norm_label: rls enabled on all tables, no policies: deny by default (2026-09-29)
nodes.rationale: Supabase exposes the public schema via its Data API with the anon key; without RLS anyone could read/write tables directly, bypassing server actions and app-level checks.

nodes.label: RLS strategy alongside Prisma: Prisma bypasses RLS, code enforces ownership (task 1.2)
nodes.norm_label: rls strategy alongside prisma: prisma bypasses rls, code enforces ownership (task 1.2)
nodes.rationale: Prisma connects as table owner so RLS policies never apply to it; splitting authorization between SQL policies and code would mean two places to maintain and test, so one path (server code with requireUser + owner checks) is the single authorization mechanism.

nodes.label: Avatar path stored, not URL; new random filename replaces old photo (task 1.14a)
nodes.norm_label: avatar path stored, not url; new random filename replaces old photo (task 1.14a)
nodes.rationale: Storing a path instead of a full URL means a future Supabase domain change doesn't break saved data; a new filename per upload avoids browser/CDN caching from serving a stale overwritten file.

nodes.label: avatars Storage bucket and RLS policies via migration (task 1.13)
nodes.norm_label: avatars storage bucket and rls policies via migration (task 1.13)
nodes.rationale: Storage access rules must live in git, pass review, and reproduce on a fresh Supabase project, so they are written as a Prisma migration rather than set by hand in the dashboard.

nodes.label: Chat: private thread per request, group thread for doubles (2026-09-24)
nodes.norm_label: chat: private thread per request, group thread for doubles (2026-09-24)
nodes.rationale: A private thread lets two people negotiate before acceptance without exposing phone/email; a group thread is needed once four accepted doubles players must coordinate.

nodes.label: CI on GitHub Actions mirrors local commands (2026-09-29)
nodes.norm_label: ci on github actions mirrors local commands (2026-09-29)
nodes.rationale: Using the exact same commands locally and in CI means 'green for me' equals 'green in CI'; next typegen is needed because .next/types doesn't exist on a clean checkout.

nodes.label: Club detail page /clubs/[id] hides empty fields (task 2.8)
nodes.norm_label: club detail page /clubs/[id] hides empty fields (task 2.8)
nodes.rationale: Showing nothing for an unknown field is better than a dash or a made-up value; the verification date is formatted in UTC because the DB column is a plain date.

nodes.label: Club markers fetched from DB per request (task 2.5)
nodes.norm_label: club markers fetched from db per request (task 2.5)
nodes.rationale: The page reads clubs on every request, not at build time, so clubs loaded via clubs:load appear without a new deploy; CI builds without a database.

nodes.label: Club list and map selection stay in sync via shared context (task 2.7)
nodes.norm_label: club list and map selection stay in sync via shared context (task 2.7)
nodes.rationale: List and map are server-rendered slots passed into a client wrapper, so props can't carry shared selection state across them; a context object does.

nodes.label: Club data loader: tsx script, upsert by slug (task 2.3)
nodes.norm_label: club data loader: tsx script, upsert by slug (task 2.3)
nodes.rationale: A TypeScript loader lets Zod validate geography/surface/URL rules in one place alongside Prisma enums rather than duplicating rules in SQL; a separate command (not prisma db seed) because club data matters in production too.

nodes.label: /clubs page: shared data for list+map, CSS-hidden toggle on mobile (task 2.6)
nodes.norm_label: /clubs page: shared data for list+map, css-hidden toggle on mobile (task 2.6)
nodes.rationale: Switching views via client state (not a ?view= URL param) avoids re-running the server query just to show the other half of the same data; CSS hiding preserves map tiles/position and list scroll position.

nodes.label: createOffer server action requires onboarded user, derives district from club (task 3.4)
nodes.norm_label: createoffer server action requires onboarded user, derives district from club (task 3.4)
nodes.rationale: An offer without a completed profile (level, name) wouldn't help anyone find a partner; taking the district from the chosen club (not the submitted value) keeps offer and club district from ever disagreeing.

nodes.label: ELO rating counts singles matches only (2026-09-24)
nodes.norm_label: elo rating counts singles matches only (2026-09-24)
nodes.rationale: Doubles ELO needs a separate pair-vs-individual rating model, added complexity with no clear MVP benefit.

nodes.label: Email fallback sender onboarding@resend.dev, no mail at all in local dev (tasks 5.1, 5.2)
nodes.norm_label: email fallback sender onboarding@resend.dev, no mail at all in local dev (tasks 5.1, 5.2)
nodes.rationale: NODE_ENV distinguishes local development (always development) from anything deployed (always production on Vercel), so only deployed environments actually call Resend, keeping manual local testing from spamming the owner's inbox.

nodes.label: Email in test mode until domain exists (2026-09-24)
nodes.norm_label: email in test mode until domain exists (2026-09-24)
nodes.rationale: No owned domain yet; Resend sandbox mode only reaches the account owner, which is sufficient while only the owner tests.

nodes.label: ESLint strictTypeChecked + no console.log (2026-09-26)
nodes.rationale: Codebase is nearly empty so the strictest ruleset costs nothing now and is easier to relax later than to tighten on finished code; console.warn/error stay as real diagnostics, console.log is banned.

nodes.label: Hosting on free tiers: Vercel Hobby + Supabase Free (2026-09-24)
nodes.norm_label: hosting on free tiers: vercel hobby + supabase free (2026-09-24)
nodes.rationale: Only the owner tests at launch and there is no monetization yet; Supabase Free may pause on inactivity which is acceptable at this stage.

nodes.label: Pre-commit hook: husky + lint-staged (2026-09-26)
nodes.rationale: Only staged files are checked so the hook stays fast as the project grows; typecheck is left out of the hook because tsc checks the whole project and would slow every commit.

nodes.label: Club map: Leaflet client-only via next/dynamic, explicit marker icon (task 2.4)
nodes.norm_label: club map: leaflet client-only via next/dynamic, explicit marker icon (task 2.4)
nodes.rationale: Leaflet touches window at import time so it cannot even be loaded on the server; the default marker icon path breaks after bundling, so each marker gets an explicit L.icon instead of a global prototype hack.

nodes.label: Login forms and email templates via RHF+Zod and token_hash links (task 1.6)
nodes.norm_label: login forms and email templates via rhf+zod and token_hash links (task 1.6)
nodes.rationale: Reusing the official Zod resolver avoids writing a custom resolver that duplicates the same logic; token_hash links work in any browser unlike PKCE codes.

nodes.label: Protected main branch: PR + green CI, squash merge (2026-09-24)
nodes.norm_label: protected main branch: pr + green ci, squash merge (2026-09-24)
nodes.rationale: Every subtask becomes one readable commit on main and broken code never lands on the main branch.

nodes.label: Initial map view fits all club markers once, on first real container size (task 2.12)
nodes.norm_label: initial map view fits all club markers once, on first real container size (task 2.12)
nodes.rationale: Fitting bounds on a hidden 0x0 mobile container would produce an unusable zoom; fitting only once avoids snapping back after the user pans or resizes.

nodes.label: Migration 3.22 applied directly, bypassing Prisma's shadow DB (2026-10-14)
nodes.norm_label: migration 3.22 applied directly, bypassing prisma's shadow db (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: prisma migrate dev fails replaying history against a shadow DB because migration 3.15's SQL uses auth.uid(), which doesn't exist in a plain Postgres shadow DB; every subsequent migration must apply directly via prisma db execute plus migrate resolve --applied until this is fixed.

nodes.label: next.config.ts sets agentRules:false (2026-09-26)
nodes.rationale: Next.js 16 dev mode auto-appends an agent-rules block into AGENTS.md when run by an AI agent, breaking the 'don't touch files outside the task' rule for a human-reviewed document.

nodes.label: Node/pnpm pinned via .nvmrc, engines, packageManager (2026-09-26)
nodes.rationale: engineStrict makes pnpm fail loudly on the wrong Node version instead of silently warning; .nvmrc/engines.node feed CI and Vercel; packageManager auto-switches pnpm version instead of warning.

nodes.label: Feed filters via GET form in URL: date, district, NTRP, format (task 3.7)
nodes.norm_label: feed filters via get form in url: date, district, ntrp, format (task 3.7)
nodes.rationale: A plain GET form lets the browser put filters in the URL so results are shareable and back navigation works, with the server doing the filtering; invalid values are ignored rather than erroring.

nodes.label: Offer format: singles default, doubles optional (2026-09-24)
nodes.norm_label: offer format: singles default, doubles optional (2026-09-24)
nodes.rationale: Singles is the main sparring scenario; linking a doubles partner to an account would complicate the model without enough benefit at launch.

nodes.label: /offers/new form: RHF raw mode, shouldUnregister for partner checkbox (task 3.5)
nodes.norm_label: /offers/new form: rhf raw mode, shouldunregister for partner checkbox (task 3.5)
nodes.rationale: raw:true keeps the client schema's Date conversion from leaking into what the server action re-parses; shouldUnregister clears the hidden partner checkbox value when switching back to singles.

nodes.label: Offer Zod schema: server interprets datetime-local as Kraków time (task 3.3)
nodes.norm_label: offer zod schema: server interprets datetime-local as krakow time (task 3.3)
nodes.rationale: The browser only knows its own timezone, and Vercel runs in UTC, so the server must fix the timezone as Europe/Warsaw rather than trusting new Date(local) on either side.

nodes.label: /offers feed: offset pagination, computed open seats, explicit select (task 3.6)
nodes.norm_label: /offers feed: offset pagination, computed open seats, explicit select (task 3.6)
nodes.rationale: A page-number URL is simple and shareable and lets filters live alongside it; open seats are computed from an accepted-count query rather than a stored column to avoid N+1 queries.

nodes.label: Unonboarded players redirected via (member) route group layout (task 1.12b)
nodes.norm_label: unonboarded players redirected via (member) route group layout (task 1.12b)
nodes.rationale: The proxy stays DB-free since it runs on every request; a shared layout for the whole (member) group is harder to forget than a per-page check.

nodes.label: Accepted plan additions: 0.22, 0.23, 1.19, 6.19 (2026-09-24)
nodes.rationale: Each addition closes a gap found during planning: branch protection enforcement, a place to write e2e tests, Resend auth-email limits, and error monitoring visibility.

nodes.label: Playwright runs against the production build (task 0.23)
nodes.norm_label: playwright runs against the production build (task 0.23)
nodes.rationale: The production build is what users get; dev mode compiles pages on the fly making tests slower and flakier; a separate port avoids colliding with pnpm dev.

nodes.label: Prettier defaults, markdown excluded, LF everywhere (2026-09-26)
nodes.norm_label: prettier defaults, markdown excluded, lf everywhere (2026-09-26)
nodes.rationale: Default settings minimize decisions/arguments; Prettier would wreck markdown task-list indentation and table width; CRLF on Windows vs LF in CI would make format:check inconsistent without eol=lf.

nodes.label: Prisma 7 setup: driver adapter, lib/db.ts single client (2026-09-28)
nodes.norm_label: prisma 7 setup: driver adapter, lib/db.ts single client (2026-09-28)
nodes.rationale: Prisma 7 clients only work via driver adapters; @prisma/adapter-pg is the official Postgres adapter; Prisma no longer reads env files itself so Node's built-in loader is used instead of dotenv.

nodes.label: Prisma Client generated in build script, not just postinstall (2026-10-03)
nodes.norm_label: prisma client generated in build script, not just postinstall (2026-10-03)
nodes.rationale: Vercel restores node_modules from cache so postinstall sometimes doesn't run; the generated client directory is gitignored and not cached, so build broke on a cached deploy without this fix.

nodes.label: Proxy protects everything except an explicit public-routes allowlist (task 1.4)
nodes.norm_label: proxy protects everything except an explicit public-routes allowlist (task 1.4)
nodes.rationale: A forgotten public page is noticed immediately (extra login redirect); a forgotten protected page silently leaks data, so the allowlist is of public pages, not protected ones.

nodes.label: RLS deny-by-default verified by e2e test, not a new migration (task 1.17)
nodes.norm_label: rls deny-by-default verified by e2e test, not a new migration (task 1.17)
nodes.rationale: Deriving the table list from the Data API's own OpenAPI output means a new table that forgot to enable RLS is automatically caught by the test.

nodes.label: Seed on plain SQL, not TypeScript (2026-09-29)
nodes.norm_label: seed on plain sql, not typescript (2026-09-29)
nodes.rationale: A TypeScript seed would need a separate runner (tsx) since Node can't execute the generated Prisma Client directly; SQL needs no new dependency and DB names are already snake_case.

nodes.label: shadcn/ui default preset on Base UI, not Radix (2026-10-01)
nodes.norm_label: shadcn/ui default preset on base ui, not radix (2026-10-01)
nodes.rationale: Default CLI settings minimize decisions, as with Prettier; Base UI is shadcn's current default and mixing two primitive libraries in one repo was rejected.

nodes.label: Sign out is local-device only; header reads session server-side (task 1.8)
nodes.norm_label: sign out is local-device only; header reads session server-side (task 1.8)
nodes.rationale: Supabase's default signOut scope is global and would log a user out everywhere; reading the session on the server avoids a sign-in/out button flicker on page load.

nodes.label: Starting ELO derived linearly from self-rated NTRP, 100 points per 0.5 NTRP (task 4.1)
nodes.norm_label: starting elo derived linearly from self-rated ntrp, 100 points per 0.5 ntrp (task 4.1)
nodes.rationale: Under the standard 400-scale ELO formula, a 100-point gap implies roughly a 64% win chance, plausible for players half an NTRP level apart; a lookup table is easier for the owner to read and change than an inline formula.

nodes.label: UI language: English only pre-i18n (2026-09-24)
nodes.rationale: One language means less MVP work; i18n added only once real need appears.

nodes.label: Unsubscribe link: GET only displays, explicit click confirms the action (task 5.3)
nodes.norm_label: unsubscribe link: get only displays, explicit click confirms the action (task 5.3)
nodes.rationale: Mail clients and security scanners sometimes prefetch links before a human sees them; if GET itself unsubscribed, such a prefetch could unsubscribe someone who never opened the email.

nodes.label: User row is created by the auth callback, not a DB trigger (task 1.9)
nodes.norm_label: user row is created by the auth callback, not a db trigger (task 1.9)
nodes.rationale: All writes to public go through Prisma and code; a trigger on auth.users would be SQL outside Prisma's managed schema and invisible to TypeScript review.

nodes.label: Vitest: explicit @/ alias, no plugins, node env (2026-09-29)
nodes.norm_label: vitest: explicit @/ alias, no plugins, node env (2026-09-29)
nodes.rationale: One alias doesn't justify a plugin dependency; restricting tests/ keeps Vitest from picking up Playwright specs in e2e/.

nodes.label: Two-strikes rule for growing AGENTS.md and decisions.md
nodes.norm_label: two-strikes rule for growing agents.md and decisions.md
nodes.rationale: A mistake is only promoted from the agent's scratch log into a permanent rule the second time it happens, keeping AGENTS.md from bloating with one-off notes.

nodes.label: Slice D: chat (messages, system messages, realtime)
nodes.norm_label: slice d: chat (messages, system messages, realtime)

nodes.label: Court booking v1: request-based booking for partner clubs, SpinBuddy-owned availability (2026-10-21)
nodes.norm_label: court booking v1: request-based booking for partner clubs, spinbuddy-owned availability (2026-10-21)
nodes.rationale: Club owner demand for in-app court availability visibility turned out higher than expected at launch; scraping third-party booking sites was rejected both for ToS violations and EU sui generis database right risk, so availability is only what a partner club itself enters into SpinBuddy.

nodes.label: Club chat: ClubFollow subscription table, RLS enabled with no policy (session O1, O.1)
nodes.norm_label: club chat: clubfollow subscription table, rls enabled with no policy (session o1, o.1)
nodes.rationale: Scoped reading for club chat (an open wall was rejected by the owner) needs an audience concept; this table exists before the chat itself because a later SECURITY DEFINER function will read it as owner to decide access.

nodes.label: Club chat: Message.clubId third thread type, RLS policy function swapped safely (session O2, O.8)
nodes.norm_label: club chat: message.clubid third thread type, rls policy function swapped safely (session o2, o.8)
nodes.rationale: Adding clubId to the existing Message row reuses Realtime, reports, data export and content checks already built for messages, instead of duplicating all of that in a second table; the new 4-argument policy function is created and switched over before the old one is deleted so the table is never without a read policy.

nodes.label: Club submissions: new inbox table + new RLS read policy via private.is_admin (slice M, M1)
nodes.norm_label: club submissions: new inbox table + new rls read policy via private.is_admin (slice m, m1)
nodes.rationale: Approval never auto-creates a Club row; the owner still verifies and loads real clubs via clubs:load, keeping the 'never invent data, always verifiedAt' discipline that already governs the Club model.

nodes.label: Club submission review queue ships without notifying the submitter (slice M, M2)
nodes.norm_label: club submission review queue ships without notifying the submitter (slice m, m2)
nodes.rationale: notify()/NotificationEvent hard-requires an offerId on every variant, and club decisions have no offer, so adding it would mean weakening the core notifications schema or building a separate channel, both out of scope for this optional task.

nodes.label: Messages model and first RLS read policy via SECURITY DEFINER function (task 3.15)
nodes.norm_label: messages model and first rls read policy via security definer function (task 3.15)
nodes.rationale: A policy subquery directly reading offer_joins/sparring_offers always saw nothing because those tables themselves deny-by-default under RLS; a SECURITY DEFINER function bypasses that correctly, and it lives in a private (non-API) schema so PostgREST can't expose it as a callable RPC oracle.

nodes.label: MVP ships without court booking system (2026-09-20)
nodes.norm_label: mvp ships without court booking system (2026-09-20)
nodes.rationale: The core value is finding a partner (matchFinder), not replacing club booking systems; booking/payments is a large separate scope that would delay launch.

nodes.label: Applying migrations to production is a manual human step (task 6.10)
nodes.norm_label: applying migrations to production is a manual human step (task 6.10)
nodes.rationale: Auto-running migrations as part of deploy would let any push to main irreversibly change the production schema without explicit in-the-moment confirmation, a risk level AGENTS.md §9 already rejects for the dev DB and production deserves at least the same discipline.

nodes.label: System messages: Message.type enum, nullable sender_id (2026-10-15)
nodes.norm_label: system messages: message.type enum, nullable sender_id (2026-10-15)
nodes.rationale: A nullable column on the same table keeps one thread, one history, one chronological order, instead of forcing the UI to merge two message sources; a CHECK ties type=SYSTEM to a null sender even for rows written outside the app code.

nodes.label: Env vars set only in Vercel dashboard, shared dev DB for preview+prod (2026-10-01)
nodes.norm_label: env vars set only in vercel dashboard, shared dev db for preview+prod (2026-10-01)
nodes.rationale: DIRECT_URL is only needed by migration CLI and must not sit where the deployed app could leak it; sharing one Supabase project for preview/production is an accepted testing-stage compromise until real users arrive.

nodes.label: Boundaries: stop-and-ask conditions (§9/§10)
nodes.rationale: A short question is cheaper than a mistake nobody will catch in an unread diff, so the agent stops only for secrets, destructive migrations, auth/payment code, bulk deletion, new external services, or a new RLS policy opening reads.

nodes.label: Slice A: sync plan with code, lighten process
nodes.norm_label: slice a: sync plan with code, lighten process

nodes.label: Slice B: finish the offer (age 18, court status)
nodes.norm_label: slice b: finish the offer (age 18, court status)

nodes.label: Slice C: request and acceptance (main loop)
nodes.norm_label: slice c: request and acceptance (main loop)

nodes.label: Slice G: courts and external booking links
nodes.norm_label: slice g: courts and external booking links

nodes.label: Author-initiated offer cancellation leaves join statuses unchanged (task 3.14)
nodes.norm_label: author-initiated offer cancellation leaves join statuses unchanged (task 3.14)
nodes.rationale: If cancellation changed join statuses, an accepted player couldn't distinguish 'I was declined' from 'the game was cancelled', so cancellation only changes the offer's own status under the same row lock as accept/decline.

nodes.label: Join accept/decline/withdraw transition table with row locking (task 3.12)
nodes.norm_label: join accept/decline/withdraw transition table with row locking (task 3.12)
nodes.rationale: Without locking the offer row with SELECT FOR UPDATE, two simultaneous accepts on the last singles seat could both succeed and over-fill the offer.

nodes.label: Minimum age 16 (superseded) (2026-09-24)
nodes.rationale: Below 16, RODO data processing needs parental consent; public age instead of birth date minimizes personal data.

nodes.label: Minimum age raised to 18 (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: The app connects strangers offline; 18+ removes the risk of adults contacting minors in person.

nodes.label: /offers/[id] page: role-specific view, actions re-validate server-side (task 3.13)
nodes.norm_label: /offers/[id] page: role-specific view, actions re-validate server-side (task 3.13)
nodes.rationale: UUID-only public route pattern keeps /offers/new out of the public template; buttons are a hint, not protection, because every action re-checks its own rules.

nodes.label: Offer invite accepted goes straight to ACCEPTED, not REQUESTED (slice S1, task S1.2)
nodes.norm_label: offer invite accepted goes straight to accepted, not requested (slice s1, task s1.2)
nodes.rationale: The author already agreed to this player the moment they sent the invite, so a second approval step adds nothing but an extra click.

nodes.label: OfferJoin request schema already covered by base schema 0.12 (task 3.10)
nodes.norm_label: offerjoin request schema already covered by base schema 0.12 (task 3.10)
nodes.rationale: Status and timestamps already existing from the base schema cover everything 3.11-3.14 need, so no new migration was required; a self-join rule between two tables belongs in a server action, not a CHECK.

nodes.label: requestToJoin server action: idempotent insert, no PII in the response (task 3.11)
nodes.norm_label: requesttojoin server action: idempotent insert, no pii in the response (task 3.11)
nodes.rationale: createMany with skipDuplicates turns a double-click race into a Postgres ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING instead of a unique-constraint error; the response is just ok/refusal text because contact happens through the private thread, not phone/email.

nodes.label: Slice Q: Play again + share button + OG preview
nodes.norm_label: slice q: play again + share button + og preview

nodes.label: Slice S1: invite a player into an offer (OfferInvite)
nodes.norm_label: slice s1: invite a player into an offer (offerinvite)

nodes.label: Slice S2: matched candidates on own offer
nodes.norm_label: slice s2: matched candidates on own offer
nodes.rationale: Depends on S1: a candidates list without an 'Invite' button would be useless, so S2 builds on S1.

nodes.label: Slice T: waitlist for a full offer (OfferWaitlist)
nodes.norm_label: slice t: waitlist for a full offer (offerwaitlist)

nodes.label: Slice U3: 'Play today' (Play Now)
nodes.rationale: Needs preferences (U1) and intents (U2) to show relevant content, otherwise it shows emptiness.

nodes.label: Slice V: automatic game suggestions (opt-in nightly cron)
nodes.norm_label: slice v: automatic game suggestions (opt-in nightly cron)
nodes.rationale: Only makes sense once player density is sufficient (target: >=150 weekly active); earlier it would propose emptiness.

nodes.label: Slice W: post-match feedback tags and achievements
nodes.norm_label: slice w: post-match feedback tags and achievements

nodes.label: Matchmaking candidates: users.discoverable defaults to true, opt-out not opt-in (slice S2, task S2.3)
nodes.norm_label: matchmaking candidates: users.discoverable defaults to true, opt-out not opt-in (slice s2, task s2.3)
nodes.rationale: Without this default, the 'Who to invite' candidate list would start empty for almost everyone; the column only hides a player from others' candidate lists and changes nothing about the feed or join requests.

nodes.label: Personal blocking: new UserBlock table, no RLS policy, bidirectional effect (slice R, R.1-R.4)
nodes.norm_label: personal blocking: new userblock table, no rls policy, bidirectional effect (slice r, r.1-r.4)
nodes.rationale: A separate table (not a column on OfferJoin/Message) reflects that blocking exists independent of any specific offer or thread; an asymmetric blocker/blocked pair gives type-safe two-way Prisma relations without a JSON array column.

nodes.label: Slice I: security and minimal admin
nodes.norm_label: slice i: security and minimal admin

nodes.label: Autoblock after 3 reports from different users within 30 days (2026-10-14)
nodes.norm_label: autoblock after 3 reports from different users within 30 days (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: Requiring distinct reporters protects against one person weaponizing the autoblock; a 30-day window prevents old reports from accumulating forever.

nodes.label: Next.js 16, Node 24 LTS, Prisma 7 versions pinned (2026-09-25)
nodes.norm_label: next.js 16, node 24 lts, prisma 7 versions pinned (2026-09-25)
nodes.rationale: Next.js 16 is current stable (15.x only gets backports); Node 24 is Active LTS through 2028 while 20/22 are aging out; Prisma 8 was only an RC so stable 7.x was chosen instead.

nodes.label: Quiet hours and daily limit drop an event rather than queue it; chat push grouping is per-thread not per-direction (2026-10-15)
nodes.norm_label: quiet hours and daily limit drop an event rather than queue it; chat push grouping is per-thread not per-direction (2026-10-15)
nodes.rationale: A deferred queue would need new state and a wake-up job; dropping the blocked event keeps zero new state, matching the session's broader preference for counters over event logs.

nodes.label: Rate limiting implementation: fixed window, one counters table (task 6.16)
nodes.norm_label: rate limiting implementation: fixed window, one counters table (task 6.16)
nodes.rationale: A sliding window without a new service would need an event log and range counting on every check; a fixed window's worst case (up to double the limit at a window boundary) is acceptable given limits are set well above normal usage.

nodes.label: Rate limiting via a Postgres counters table, no new service (2026-10-14)
nodes.norm_label: rate limiting via a postgres counters table, no new service (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: A counters table in the same database avoids adding a new infrastructure dependency (e.g. Redis) just for rate limiting at this scale.

nodes.label: Reports and admin schema: targetUserId always resolved server-side (tasks 3.19, 6.1-6.4)
nodes.norm_label: reports and admin schema: targetuserid always resolved server-side (tasks 3.19, 6.1-6.4)
nodes.rationale: Normalizing targetUserId at write time is the only way both autoblock and the moderation queue avoid repeating the same offerId->authorId or messageId->senderId join on every read; /admin returns the same 404 to anonymous and non-admin visitors to avoid revealing route existence via a login redirect.

nodes.label: Project stack decision (2026-09-20)
nodes.rationale: One framework for front+back, one managed service instead of separate DB/auth/storage/realtime, free tiers suffice at launch, OpenStreetMap avoids Google Maps keys/limits, Zod schema shared between form and server.

nodes.label: Slice E: match result and ELO
nodes.norm_label: slice e: match result and elo

nodes.label: Slice F: player reliability (no-show, late cancellation)
nodes.norm_label: slice f: player reliability (no-show, late cancellation)

nodes.label: ELO formula: E=1/(1+10^((Rb-Ra)/400)), K=40 for first 10 matches then 20, floor 100 (2026-10-14)
nodes.norm_label: elo formula: e=1/(1+10^((rb-ra)/400)), k=40 for first 10 matches then 20, floor 100 (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: The standard ELO formula with a variable K lets a new player's rating find its correct level faster while match history is still thin.

nodes.label: MatchResult model: jsonb score, winner/reportedBy enum, ELO snapshots (task 4.4)
nodes.norm_label: matchresult model: jsonb score, winner/reportedby enum, elo snapshots (task 4.4)
nodes.rationale: winner/reportedBy use an AUTHOR/PLAYER enum rather than a user-id FK because the two sides are always unambiguous via offer_join_id; a CHECK ties the four ELO snapshot columns to CONFIRMED status so a crash mid-transaction can't leave a half-applied result.

nodes.label: No-show result: noShowParty field, nullable score, manual confirm refused (task 4.10)
nodes.norm_label: no-show result: noshowparty field, nullable score, manual confirm refused (task 4.10)
nodes.rationale: Reusing submitResultRefusal avoids duplicating the same participant/singles/accepted/started/no-result conditions for score vs no-show; a separate table would force two other modules to merge two data sources over one nullable column, the same reasoning already used for system message type.

nodes.label: Player reliability: late cancellation under 12h, no-show flag, reliability shown after 3 scheduled matches (2026-10-14)
nodes.norm_label: player reliability: late cancellation under 12h, no-show flag, reliability shown after 3 scheduled matches (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: 12 hours gives enough time to find a replacement; showing reliability only after 3 matches avoids one random mishap looking like a systemic problem for a new player.

nodes.label: Reliability counters stored as User fields, not derived from a query (tasks 4.11-4.12)
nodes.norm_label: reliability counters stored as user fields, not derived from a query (tasks 4.11-4.12)
nodes.rationale: offer_joins only stores the current status, so a withdrawn or cancelled join would undercount a scheduled match that should still count against reliability, and there is no history at all for a late cancellation; the same argument that already made matchesPlayed a counter.

nodes.label: Match result confirmation: opponent confirms, auto-confirm after 72h, dispute goes to admin (2026-10-14)
nodes.norm_label: match result confirmation: opponent confirms, auto-confirm after 72h, dispute goes to admin (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: Without auto-confirmation, a vanished opponent would block ELO updates forever; 72 hours gives enough time to respond without delaying rating updates too long.

nodes.label: Score format: 2-3 sets, super-tiebreak to 10 in third set (2026-10-14)
nodes.norm_label: score format: 2-3 sets, super-tiebreak to 10 in third set (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: This mirrors standard amateur tennis scoring; a third-set super-tiebreak is a popular amateur compromise to avoid a full third set.

nodes.label: Account deletion: manual owner-run process, no self-service button (superseded) (2026-10-16)
nodes.norm_label: account deletion: manual owner-run process, no self-service button (superseded) (2026-10-16)
nodes.rationale: The owner, after seeing a self-service UI plan, chose instead to perform deletions manually and rarely via documented SQL steps, since existing code already handles blank names/emails gracefully.

nodes.label: Account deletion: profile/photo/email/birthdate redacted, confirmed matches kept with 'Deleted player' (2026-10-14)
nodes.norm_label: account deletion: profile/photo/email/birthdate redacted, confirmed matches kept with 'deleted player' (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: Matches history must stay consistent with the 2026-09-28 Restrict-on-results decision so an opponent's ELO history never depends on whether the other player deleted their account.

nodes.label: Account deletion: self-service button replaces the manual process (2026-10-16)
nodes.norm_label: account deletion: self-service button replaces the manual process (2026-10-16)
nodes.rationale: The owner reconsidered after seeing the ready manual process and wanted a button instead of running SQL on every request; this is the first app code (not just e2e) to read SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY, an explicit amendment to the RLS strategy's 'only e2e uses service_role' rule.

nodes.label: Base DB schema: conventions and delete rules (2026-09-28)
nodes.norm_label: base db schema: conventions and delete rules (2026-09-28)
nodes.rationale: snake_case keeps hand-written RLS/SQL readable; UUID ids avoid enumeration via URLs; no FK to auth.users because Prisma manages only the public schema; Restrict on match results protects opponents' ELO history from silent deletion.

nodes.label: ELO and matches_played stored on User, editable only before first match (task 4.2)
nodes.norm_label: elo and matches_played stored on user, editable only before first match (task 4.2)
nodes.rationale: Before any match, ELO is just another form of NTRP, so editing NTRP in the profile should move it; after the first confirmed match only match results may move the rating, enforced by an atomic update guarded on matches_played=0.

nodes.label: Leaderboard v1: read-only ELO ranking, no season model (2026-10-30)
nodes.norm_label: leaderboard v1: read-only elo ranking, no season model (2026-10-30)
nodes.rationale: Reusing already-collected data (User.elo, matchesPlayed, district) fits the whole feature in one slice; a full challenge-based seasonal ladder is deferred to a future epic pending proof that people look at this page.

nodes.label: Player profile fields: district enum, gender, self-rated NTRP (task 1.10)
nodes.norm_label: player profile fields: district enum, gender, self-rated ntrp (task 1.10)
nodes.rationale: NTRP is a Float not Decimal because Prisma's Decimal can't pass directly to a client component; CHECK constraints keep data valid even if a row is written outside app code.

nodes.label: Analytics and Sentry implementation details (tasks 6.5, 6.6, 6.19)
nodes.rationale: posthog-node (not posthog-js) is used because every tracked event starts in a server action, so there is no client SDK and thus no cookie to worry about; Sentry's documented sendDefaultPii/disableLogger options don't exist in the installed version's types, so a shared beforeSend scrubber achieves the same PII-free result explicitly in code.

nodes.label: Language: English + Polish before public launch, Ukrainian deferred (2026-10-14)
nodes.norm_label: language: english + polish before public launch, ukrainian deferred (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: Polish players are the main Kraków audience; Ukrainian is deferred to avoid doubling translation volume before launch.

nodes.label: Legal pages as Draft placeholders, consent captured at onboarding (tasks 6.11, 6.12)
nodes.norm_label: legal pages as draft placeholders, consent captured at onboarding (tasks 6.11, 6.12)
nodes.rationale: requireOnboardedUser() already gates every page under onboarding, so routing consent through the same mechanism automatically covers every page without a second route list in the proxy.

nodes.label: Polish language via next-intl, cookie-only locale, no URL prefix (task 1.20)
nodes.norm_label: polish language via next-intl, cookie-only locale, no url prefix (task 1.20)
nodes.rationale: No URL prefix was an explicit prior decision to minimize route changes, so next-intl runs in cookie-only mode rather than its [locale]-segment routing; the locale lives in a cookie for rendering (avoiding a DB query per request) and mirrored to users.locale only for async mailing jobs that have no request cookie.

nodes.label: Analytics: PostHog EU, cookie-free mode (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: EU region keeps data inside the EU; memory persistence sets no cookie, so no legal requirement for a cookie banner.

nodes.label: Staging/production split deferred until first real users (2026-10-14)
nodes.norm_label: staging/production split deferred until first real users (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: While only the owner tests, one shared database is an acceptable time-saving compromise; splitting is real work (a new Supabase project, data migration) not worth doing yet.

nodes.label: Club fields: surfaces array, indoor enum, slug, verified_at (task 2.1)
nodes.norm_label: club fields: surfaces array, indoor enum, slug, verified_at (task 2.1)
nodes.rationale: A Kraków club often has multiple surfaces and partial winter cover, so surfaces is an array and indoor cover is a separate field; slug is a stable upsert key independent of DB-generated id; verified_at tells players how fresh the data is.

nodes.label: Club schema extended for real collected data; no test club in shared DB (task 2.11)
nodes.norm_label: club schema extended for real collected data; no test club in shared db (task 2.11)
nodes.rationale: NULL/empty list means 'unknown' rather than a fabricated placeholder value; a test club was rejected because dev/preview/production share one database that every visitor to /clubs would see.

nodes.label: Cron: Vercel daily cron now, GitHub Actions schedule for hourly later (task 5.8)
nodes.norm_label: cron: vercel daily cron now, github actions schedule for hourly later (task 5.8)
nodes.rationale: GitHub Actions is already in the stack for CI so adding a schedule workflow is not a new external service, unlike enabling Supabase pg_cron/pg_net, which would need new Postgres extensions and a new way to call an HTTP endpoint for the same result.

nodes.label: Web push is the primary notification channel, email is a fallback (2026-10-14)
nodes.norm_label: web push is the primary notification channel, email is a fallback (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: Push needs no domain or mail provider and is less likely to land in spam; email fallback covers players without the PWA installed or who denied the push permission.

nodes.label: Notification schema: PushSubscription table, settings toggles, users.email mirror column (tasks 5.3, 5.15, 5.16)
nodes.norm_label: notification schema: pushsubscription table, settings toggles, users.email mirror column (tasks 5.3, 5.15, 5.16)
nodes.rationale: users.email is needed because email fallback must write to someone, but public.users never stored email and the app can't read auth.users without the secret key reserved for e2e; a mirrored column updated on every login is the smallest change that avoids that restriction.

nodes.label: Hourly reminders via the same /api/cron endpoint with job=reminders (tasks 5.8, 5.10, 5.16)
nodes.norm_label: hourly reminders via the same /api/cron endpoint with job=reminders (tasks 5.8, 5.10, 5.16)
nodes.rationale: One external action (a curl with a secret) is reused instead of inventing a new way to run code or a new Postgres extension.

nodes.label: Offer and chat model: author is implicit participant, formula for players needed (task 3.1)
nodes.norm_label: offer and chat model: author is implicit participant, formula for players needed (task 3.1)
nodes.rationale: Keeping the author and their marked partner out of OfferJoin avoids excluding partner-less requests from seat counts, ELO and chat logic; a derived player-count function can't drift from the data the way a stored count could.

nodes.label: Offer court status: BOOKED/WILL_BOOK/ANY, default WILL_BOOK (2026-10-14)
nodes.norm_label: offer court status: booked/will_book/any, default will_book (2026-10-14)
nodes.rationale: Authors don't always book a court in advance; some agree on the game first and book afterward, so the most common scenario is the default.

nodes.label: Offer duration_minutes field with fixed allowed values (2026-10-17)
nodes.norm_label: offer duration_minutes field with fixed allowed values (2026-10-17)
nodes.rationale: Players book courts in fixed blocks, so a fixed list (60/90/120/180) gives a clean filter rather than arbitrary minutes; default 90 backfills old offers with no migration needed.

nodes.label: Offer fields: NTRP range, surface, district/club with one required (task 3.2)
nodes.norm_label: offer fields: ntrp range, surface, district/club with one required (task 3.2)
nodes.rationale: Existing rows are backfilled by the migration itself so it applies cleanly in any environment without manual cleanup; 'starts in the future' can't be a CHECK because it depends on the current time, so Zod enforces it instead.
